key_insight: CRISP uses stable probability rankings under domain shift to build robust high-precision and high-recall spatial priors for segmentation without test-time adaptation or target data.
clinical_relevance: It may improve the reliability of medical image segmentation across unseen hospitals, patient groups, and imaging modalities, where standard models often fail.
method: Perturbs latent features to identify invariant high-grade regions as a high-precision core.
Finds voxels that stay potentially foreground across perturbations to form a high-recall support.
Iteratively squeezes these priors toward the final mask during training, using a frozen-weight, plug-in refinement framework.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on multi-center cardiac MRI and CT lung vessel segmentation, with reported HD95 improvements up to 7.0%, 13.1%, and 38.9% across multi-center, demographic, and modality shifts.
watch_item: Its robustness depends on the assumption that positive-region rankings remain stable under shift, which may not hold uniformly across all datasets or pathological cases.
paper_title: CRISP: Constrained Refinement via Iterative Squeezing Process for Robust Medical Image Segmentation under Domain Shift
